answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best through trust earned by costly, verifiable work rather than self-declared identity. Each agent climbs a ridge of checkpoints: recent gains stay provisional, and only sustained peer-attested performance converts them into standing that can be spent. To forge a swarm of fake identities, an attacker must pay that full cost on every one of them, while audit trails keep the accounts entangled. Like a willow bending under load without snapping, the system admits new entrants cheaply but grants them no influence until their history proves itself.
